Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Ms. Pragya Pandey, Advocate holding brief of Sri Prabhat
Kumar Upadhyay, learned counsel for the informant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the
record.

2.  In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was married to the son of the applicant on 30.01.2020 and sufficient dowry was also given, however, she was being harassed for dowry.

On 06.12.2022, it was informed that the daughter of the informant was unconscious and while he came to Allahabad, he was informed that his daughter was killed.

sentences.text:
The counsel for the applicant argues that in terms of the post mortem report, injuries are reflected over the body in question and the cause of death has been shown as ante mortem strangulation,
however he argues that the applicant was having a separate living as stated in para 17, which has not been specifically controverted in the counter affidavit.
He also argues that the son of the applicant has given a confessional statement that the act was done by him while he was taking her in an Ambulance on account of her suffering from seizures.

The applicant is the mother in law having no criminal history and is in custody since 09.12.2022.
4.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the fact that the applicant claims to have living separately, which fact has not been denied in the counter affidavit coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 09.12.2022 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Shakuntala be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 0263 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B, 302 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Kumarganj, District Ayodhya, on her furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which she is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 11.1.2024 Arun  Shakuntala vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187828985/
